claims.text: The initial alloy is near Ti 30 at%, Ni 30 at%, Nb 10 at%, Mo 10 at%, and Cr 10 at%.
The stated composition maintains the high-entropy-alloy compositional criteria.
The initial alloy has a single-phase homogeneous matrix.
The intervention adds 1–2 wt% surface-treated Y2O3 nanoparticles by high-energy ball milling, followed by HIP at 1000°C for 2 hours and annealing at 750°C.
Surface treatment and optimized ball milling will produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion of Y2O3 throughout the alloy matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will remain thermally stable during processing and testing at 700–800°C.
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as pinning centers that inhibit dislocation motion.
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles pin grain boundaries and inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Inhibition of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will improve creep resistance and elevated-temperature yield strength.
At 700–800°C, the Y2O3-modified alloy will have approximately 20–30% greater yield strength than the identically processed alloy without Y2O3.
At 700–800°C, the Y2O3-modified alloy will have a lower creep rate than the identically processed alloy without Y2O3.
The improvement applies only when milling, HIP, and annealing avoid destabilizing the alloy phases.
Nonuniform or unstable Y2O3 dispersion would reduce the strengthening effect.
Interfacial reactions during high-temperature processing could reduce the efficacy of Y2O3 strengthening.

contradictions.description: The listed elemental concentrations total only 90 at%, so they do not specify a complete alloy composition even though the hypothesis characterizes them as satisfying the stated compositional limits. The missing 10 at% also prevents verification that every constituent lies within 5–35 at%.

The prediction specifies a 20–30% yield-strength increase, whereas the falsification rule uses an approximate 10–20% minimum. These overlapping ranges leave some results without an unambiguous relationship to the stated prediction.
